Currently, the ArkMQ Broker Operator applies the ActiveMQArtemis label to all managed resources. While this is appropriate for resources generated by the deprecated ActiveMQArtemis Custom Resources (CRs), it should not be applied to resources generated by the newer Broker CRs.

Managed resources should dynamically reflect the type of CR that created them to prevent confusion and ensure proper resource tracking.

Current Behavior
All managed resources, regardless of whether they are created via an ActiveMQArtemis CR or a Broker CR, are tagged with the ActiveMQArtemis label.

Expected Behavior
Deprecated ActiveMQArtemis CRs: Managed resources should continue to use the ActiveMQArtemis label to maintain backwards compatibility.

New Broker CRs: Managed resources must use the Broker label.

When a broker is restarted during active message flow, messages can be silently lost. The broker does not redeliver these messages to the subscriber after reconnection. It happens to messages published close to restart.

Some messages are also duplicated.

This violates the MQTT 5.0 specification, which states that QoS 2 guarantees exactly-once delivery. 

Steps to Reproduce

# Start the broker with an MQTT acceptor
# Start a subscriber 
# Start a publisher 
# During publishing, restart the broker several times (better chance to see the issue, it does not happen on every restart)
# After all messages are published, compare published vs received message IDs.


We used attached publisher and subscriber.
You can start subscriber with parameters: 

{noformat}python3 subscribe-file.py subscriber_out.txt subscriber.log{noformat}

Start publisher:

{noformat}python3 publish-file.py test_data.txt{noformat}

The test data ({{test_data.txt}}) is also attached.

After the test, please compare the output files of both the publisher and the subscriber. Exactly 10,000 messages should be delivered to the subscriber, but there are duplicates and missing messages. Both of these behaviors violate QoS 2.

The {{case2.zip}} file contains information about the test that was run on OpenShift. The logs from this test show some issues with the broker journal during restart, though these might not always appear.

Please note that to simplify the setup, the attached clients were also run directly on a single machine rather than on OpenShift. The issue was successfully replicated on a single machine.

While running the plugin locally against the OpenShift Console {{latest}} image, routing breaks due to a React Router mismatch. The console team confirmed that console {{latest}} container image is not built from *latest main branch* and still uses an older React Router stack, which is incompatible with the newer routing changes (React Router v7).

To avoid this, we should pin a specific console version instead of latest. OCP 4.22 and 4.23 are the versions that work correctly with the React Router v7 upgrade.

We currently use {{4.22-latest}} for our SDK dependencies. Since 4.23 is available, is fully backward compatible with 4.22, and other plugins are already on it, upgrading to {{4.23}} is the best option and should fix the local routing issue.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* {{@openshift-console/dynamic-plugin-sdk update from 4.22-latest to 4.23.0-prerelease.2}}
* {{@openshift-console/dynamic-plugin-sdk-webpack update from 4.22-latest to 4.23.0-prerelease.1}}
* Local console image in {{start-console.sh}} pin to {{4.22.0}} instead of {{latest}} for React Router v7 compatibility (4.23 console image not yet available on quay).
* Plugin runs locally without routing breakage

*Attachments:* Screenshots of the routing breakage when using the {{latest}} console image.

!Screenshot From 2026-06-23 17-24-06.png|width=671,alt="Screenshot From 2026-06-23 17-24-06.png"!

While running the plugin locally against the OpenShift Console *latest* image, routing breaks due to a React Router mismatch. The console team confirmed that console latest container image is not built from *latest main branch* and still uses an older React Router stack, which is incompatible with the newer routing changes (React Router v7).

To avoid this, we should pin a specific console version instead of latest. {{OCP 4.22}} and {{4.23}} are the versions that work correctly with the React Router v7 upgrade.

We initially used 4.22-latest for SDK dependencies and considered upgrading to 4.23 prerelease, since other plugin teams are moving in that direction and 4.23 is described as backward compatible with 4.22.

After discussion with the OpenShift Console team, we aligned on stable 4.22.0 GA instead:

SDK version should match the declared minimum supported Console version (@console/pluginAPI: >=4.22.0-0).
4.23 is not GA yet — only prerelease SDK packages are available.
Using 4.22-latest can resolve to prerelease builds rather than stable 4.22.0 in yarn.lock.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Pin @openshift-console/dynamic-plugin-sdk to 4.22.0 (GA)
* Pin @openshift-console/dynamic-plugin-sdk-webpack to 4.22.0 (GA)
* Pin local Console image in start-console.sh to 4.22.0 instead of latest
* README documents minimum OpenShift 4.22 or higher
* Plugin runs locally without routing breakage

*Resolution*: Pin SDK packages and the local Console image to 4.22.0 (GA) for pluginAPI alignment and React Router v7 routing compatibility. Revisit the 4.23 upgrade when 4.23.0 GA is released.

*Attachments:* Screenshots of the routing breakage when using the {{latest}} console image.

!Screenshot From 2026-06-23 17-24-06.png|width=671,alt="Screenshot From 2026-06-23 17-24-06.png"!

items.toString: Add ability to monitor total size of wildcard queues / addresses

items.fromString:
*Background:* Wildcard addresses are frequently used in MQTT setups. However, it is currently not possible to monitor the total message payload size for a wildcard queue (and therefore its address) because wildcard queues might contain only references or pointers. For more information, see: [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ENTMQBR-10599|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ENTMQBR-10599|smart-link] 

*Requested Enhancement:* Introduce a new configuration parameter that allows the broker to report the actual size of wildcard addresses, including wildcard queues that hold only message references. To achieve this, the broker would need to calculate the size by following these references to get the true size of the underlying messages they point to.

*Implementation Notes:*

* *Related Issue:* This request is closely related to [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ENTMQBR-10643|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ENTMQBR-10643|smart-link] . Ultimately, this RFE should allow users to monitor how much of that limit has been consumed by individual wildcard addresses.
* *Deduplication:* There is no need to duplicate the reported size if multiple queues point to the same underlying message. The wildcard queue/address should calculate the payload size of these shared messages only once. However, this deduplication logic will ultimately depend on how the limit is calculated in ENTMQBR-10643.

# *Broker Settings:* Add the following broker settings:
{noformat}<address-setting match="TEST.#">
  <auto-delete-addresses>true</auto-delete-addresses>
</address-setting>{noformat}
*Steps to Reproduce:*
## Attach an MQTT durable subscriber that uses a wildcard queue ({{TEST.#}}). This queue will survive a broker restart.
## Disconnect the subscriber; the queue remains.
## Connect an MQTT producer that sends (for example) 10 messages to {{TEST.1}}. The address {{TEST.1}} is created.
## Check the broker console: according to the console, the queue {{TEST.#}} is bound to address {{TEST.1}}. Because of this binding, the address should not be auto-deleted.
## Restart the broker and observe that the address {{TEST.1}} is gone. The queue {{TEST.#}} is still present on the broker (as is the {{TEST.#}} address).
# *Analysis / Possible Causes:* This behavior indicates one of two underlying issues:
## *Console Bug:* The queue {{TEST.#}} is not actually bound to the {{TEST.1}} address (but only to the {{TEST.#}} address, which survives the restart). If this is the case, there is a bug in the console incorrectly reporting attached queues and showing the {{TEST.#}} queue in the address attributes for {{TEST.1}}.
## *Auto-delete Bug:* The queue {{TEST.#}} _is_ bound to {{TEST.1}}, but the auto-delete function is not working as expected (it should not delete addresses that still have bound queues).

Can the address size be reported for wildcard addresses in MQTT?

For example, suppose there are three addresses: {{ADR.ONE.#}}, {{ADR.ONE.*.*}}, and {{ADR.ONE.TEST.TEST}}. If an MQTT producer sends messages to {{ADR.ONE.TEST.TEST}}, the broker reports an address size that seems correct.

However, {{ADR.ONE.#}} reports a size of 0 (as it has no consumers), and {{ADR.ONE.*.*}}, which was created by subscriber, reports only a very small address size (presumably pointers or references to the messages in {{ADR.ONE.TEST.TEST}}).

Should the correct address size also be reported for all wildcard addresses, like {{ADR.ONE.#}} and {{ADR.ONE.*.*}}, or is this not possible? The attached queue for {{ADR.ONE.*.*}} reports the correct number of messages, but we would also like to know the actual size of the messages there (rather than a small number that might just be references).

h2. Overview

AMQ Broker 7.14 introduces a new AMQP bridge feature for broker connections (upstream [ARTEMIS-5437|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARTEMIS-5437]) that allows bidirectional message bridging between the local broker and remote AMQP 1.0 peers.

h2. Feature Details

The AMQP bridge supports four policy types:

# *bridge-from-address* - Pull messages from remote addresses based on local demand
# *bridge-from-queue* - Pull messages from remote queues based on local demand  
# *bridge-to-address* - Send messages to remote addresses when local address exists
# *bridge-to-queue* - Send messages to remote queues when local queue exists

h3. Key Capabilities

* Works with any AMQP 1.0 peer (not just Artemis brokers)
* Supports wildcard address matching with include/exclude patterns
* Configurable priority, filters, and remote address mappings
* Durable subscription support (ARTEMIS-5476)
* Comprehensive management and monitoring via JMX

h2. Configuration Example

{code:xml}[broker-connections]
  [amqp-connection uri="tcp://HOST:PORT" name="bridge-example"]
    [bridge name="example-bridge"]
       [bridge-from-address name="example-bridge-from-address-policy"]
         [include address-match="local-address.#" /]
         [exclude address-match="local-address.excluded" /]
       [/bridge-from-address]
       [bridge-to-address name="example-bridge-to-address-policy"]
         [include address-match="outgoing-address" /]
       [/bridge-to-address]
    [/bridge]
  [/amqp-connection]
[/broker-connections]{code}

h2. Documentation Requirements

* Update broker connections documentation to include AMQP bridge section
* Provide configuration examples for all four policy types
* Document configuration attributes and their purposes
* Add use case examples (e.g., integration with Interconnect, non-Artemis AMQP peers)
* Document management and monitoring capabilities
* Note version availability (7.14+, not available in 7.13)

h2. Related Work

* Upstream: [https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARTEMIS-5437|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARTEMIS-5437]
* Durable subscriptions: [https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARTEMIS-5476|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARTEMIS-5476]
* Commit: 455c020465 (April 23, 2025)

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Product documentation includes comprehensive AMQP bridge section
* [ ] All four bridge policy types are documented with examples
* [ ] Configuration attributes are fully documented
* [ ] Version availability is clearly stated (7.14+)
* [ ] Use cases and integration scenarios are provided
* [ ] Management/monitoring capabilities are documented
